nodes.label: desktop memory - the graph is references, not copies

Frozen copy taken 2026-08-03 of the desktop machine's memory file - the live directory sits on the other machine and is not reachable from here, so this copy is what there is to review. Listed unreviewed in REVIEW_REGISTER.md section 6. The graph is an index of references over the raw source; it does not hold copies of the data, and especially not mutated or rendered copies. The user stated this directly on 2026-05-30 as the reason he never wanted content loaded into the graph: 'thats the fucking reason i dont even want the data loaded into the goddamn graph, thats why i just want the fucking references.' The model: raw source files are authoritative and untouched, the single source of truth; the graph stores references - file_id plus a real resolvable location into the raw file, a byte span or a structural path - plus the derived semantic layer of tags, weights and grounding vectors; content is resolved on demand by reading the referenced span from the untouched source, so the graph never becomes a second copy that silently replaces the original; and tags, weights and vectors attach to the reference, so nothing the pipeline does can mutate or lose the original. The root failure it fixes: the v1 chunker consumed the source, rendered it into a prose string, stored the string as c.content, and that lossy derivative became the only surviving copy - with concrete proof in the HERB path writing every chunk with start_offset=0 and end_offset=len(content), locating a position inside the fabrication rather than inside the raw file. The reference triple decided 2026-05-30 is {file_id, scheme, address}, with scheme chosen by data shape - nested JSON to json_pointer, RFC 6901.
